dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرَّاجِفَةُ) In al-Mukhtār: «al-rajfa is the earthquake; the earth rajafat, of the pattern of naṣara.» More of its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(الرَّادِفَةُ) The one that follows. In al-Qāmūs: «radifahu, like samiʿahu and naṣarahu: he followed him, like ardafahu.»
(الْحافِرَةِ) The first state; they mean life after death. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the true sense of this word? I say: one says "so-and-so returned in his ḥāfira", i.e. on his path by which he came, which he dug (ḥafarahā), i.e. left marks on by his walking in it; the marks of his feet were made a digging, just as it is said "his teeth were dug (ḥafarat), ḥafran" when decay has left its mark at their roots, and the line dug into rock. And it was called ḥāfira as it was said ʿīsha rāḍiya (a pleasing life), i.e. ascribed to digging and to pleasure, or as in their saying "your day is fasting". Then it was said of one who was in a matter, left it, and then returned to it: "he returned to his ḥāfira", i.e. to his way and his first state. He said:
أحافرة على صلع وشيب ... معاذ الله من سفه وعار»
(Back to the old ways, despite baldness and grey hair? Allah forbid such folly and shame!)
Ibn al-Aʿrābī recited it. The hamza is for disapproval. al-ḥāfira originally is the road dug by travel, so calling it ḥāfira is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), or it is in the sense of ascription, i.e. possessing digging; then it was used for every state you were in and then returned to. It is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. «shall I return ḥāfira», i.e. to my first way of youth and boyish love; or by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «shall I return to it». And al-ṣalaʿ is the receding of the hair of the forehead, and it mostly occurs in old age.
(الساهرة) The white, level land. It was named so because the mirage runs on it, from their saying ʿan sāhira [Translator's note: so in the source; probably «عين ساهرة», "a wakeful spring"] for flowing water, and for its opposite nāʾima (sleeping). Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said:
وساهرة يضحي السراب مجللا ... لأقطارها قد جئتها متلثما
(Many a wakeful waste, whose sides the mirage comes to cover by forenoon, I have come to with my face veiled.)

* I'rab:
(وَالنَّازِعاتِ غَرْقاً، وَالنَّاشِطاتِ نَشْطاً، وَالسَّابِحاتِ سَبْحاً، فَالسَّابِقاتِ سَبْقاً، فَالْمُدَبِّراتِ أَمْراً) The wāw is the wāw of the oath. He, the Exalted, swore by the groups of angels that draw out the souls from the bodies. The answer to the oath by these things by which Allah swore is omitted, i.e. «by those that draw out, and so and so, you will surely be resurrected». As for غرقا, it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with omission of the added letters, meaning إغراقا, made accusative by what precedes it because it meets it in meaning, or by an omitted verb; or else as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. possessing thoroughness. Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «غرقا is a maṣdar according to the meaning, because the one who draws (al-nāziʿ) is the one who goes to the utmost in drawing the arrow or in pulling out the soul; and it is a maṣdar with the addition omitted, i.e. إغراقا.» And al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «He, Glorified is He, swore by the groups of angels that draw out the souls from the bodies», until he says: «غرقا: going to the utmost in drawing, i.e. they draw them out from the farthest reaches of the bodies.» And it is said النازعات are horses: He swore by the horses of the raiders, which strain at their reins with a straining in which the reins are pulled to the full because of the length of their necks, since they are pure Arabians. والناشطات نشطا is conjoined to والنازعات غرقا, and likewise His saying والسابحات سبحا. In al-Mukhtār: «al-sibāḥa, with kasra, is swimming; sabaḥa, yasbaḥu, with fatḥa; and al-sabḥ is free time; and al-sabḥ is also going about one's livelihood; and its pattern is qaṭaʿa and qatala.» فالسابقات سبقا is conjoined to what preceded, and likewise فالمدبرات أمرا. The fāʾ in both indicates their sequence without delay. أمرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of المدبرات, and the answer of these oaths is omitted, as has preceded. (يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الرَّاجِفَةُ) يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted answer; you may also attach it to what is indicated by His coming saying «قلوب يومئذ واجفة», i.e. on the day the quaking quakes, the hearts tremble. The clause ترجف الراجفة is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ) The clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of الراجفة, i.e. it quakes, the follower following it; and الرادفة is the fāʿil (agent) of تتبعها. (قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ واجِفَةٌ أَبْصارُها خاشِعَةٌ) قلوب is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what licensed beginning with an indefinite noun is that it is qualified. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to واجفة; واجفة is a naʿt (adjective) of قلوب. أبصارها is a subject and خاشعة the khabar (predicate) of أبصارها, and the nominal clause is the predicate of قلوب. The eyes were annexed to the hearts with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the eyes of their owners. (يَقُولُونَ أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي الْحافِرَةِ) The clause is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. they say. يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and an agent. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, because they rejected the return and denied it. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); مردودون is the predicate of إنّا; في الحافرة is attached to مردودون, and في means إلى, i.e. to the ḥāfira. It may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl, with «في» retaining its meaning, the meaning of الحافرة being the earth in which their graves are; and the meaning is: shall we be returned while we are in the ḥāfira? What follows is al-Rāghib's wording about al-ḥāfira: «His saying في الحافرة is a proverb for one who is returned whence he came, i.e. shall we be returned to life after we die? And it is said al-ḥāfira is the earth in which their graves are, and its meaning is: shall we be returned while we are in the ḥāfira, i.e. in the graves; and His saying في الحافرة on this view is in the position of a ḥāl. And it is said "so-and-so returned upon his ḥāfira", and "the old man returned to his ḥāfira", i.e. he became decrepit, as in His saying, the Exalted: ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر. And al-ḥāfira, it is said, is fāʿila in the sense of mafʿūla; and it is said it is by way of ascription, i.e. possessing digging, and what is meant is the earth; and the meaning is: shall we be returned in our graves alive? And it is said al-ḥāfira is the plural of ḥāfir in the sense of foot, i.e. shall we walk alive on our feet and tread the earth with them?» (أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً نَخِرَةً) The interrogative is an emphasis of the content of the rejection and denial of the return, by relating it to a state incompatible with it. إذا is a future adverb, and what governs it is indicated by مردودون, i.e. when we are decayed bones, shall we be returned and resurrected, despite our being the farthest of things from life? (قالُوا تِلْكَ إِذاً كَرَّةٌ خاسِرَةٌ) A resumed statement presented to relate another disbelief branching from their previous disbelief. تلك is the subject, the reference being to the return and the restoration in the ḥāfira; إذا is a particle of answer and consequence with no governing effect, brought to convey emphasis of the losing return; كرة is the predicate of تلك and خاسرة an adjective of كرة. (فَإِنَّما هِيَ زَجْرَةٌ واحِدَةٌ) The fāʾ is connected with an omitted element whose meaning is: do not deem it hard, for it is only a single cry; meaning: do not think the return difficult for Allah the Exalted, for it is easy and light by His power, the Exalted. إنما is the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); هي is the subject, زجرة the predicate and واحدة an adjective of زجرة, i.e. a single blast. The blast (al-nafḥa [Translator's note: so in the source, for al-nafkha]) was named a cry (zajra) because from it is understood a prohibition of holding back and lagging behind it. (فَإِذا هُمْ بِالسَّاهِرَةِ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. so when it is blown...; إذا is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and the discussion of it has preceded. هم is the subject and بالساهرة the predicate.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «يوم ترجف الراجفة» there is a predicative trope (majāz isnādī): He made the cause of the quaking a quaker. In al-Qurṭubī: «The origin of al-rajfa is movement; Allah the Exalted said: يوم ترجف الأرض. And al-rajfa here is not from movement only, but from their saying: the thunder rajafa, yarjufu, rajfan and rajīfan, i.e. it produced sound and movement; and from it the alarming rumours (al-arājīf) were named, because of the agitation of voices with them and people's plunging into them.»
2- And in His saying «تلك إذا كرة خاسرة» there is a predicative trope: He ascribed the loss to the return while its people are meant; the meaning is: if our return to the Resurrection is true, then that return is a losing return.
3- Likewise in His saying «فإذا هم بالساهرة» wakefulness was ascribed to the white land figuratively, just as they ascribed sleep to its opposite. Al-Ashʿath ibn Qays said:
وساهرة يضحي السراب مجللا ... لأقطارها قد جبتها متلثما
(Many a wakeful waste, whose sides the mirage comes to cover by forenoon, I have crossed with my face veiled.)
al-sāhira is the white land, because the mirage runs on it; it was described with wakefulness because the traveller in it is wakeful and does not sleep for fear of perishing, so it is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī). مجللا is the predicate of يضحي, i.e. covering its regions and sides. He says: many a desert which the day covers with a mirage resembling a horse's rope [Translator's note: so in the source («حبل الفرس»); possibly «جلّ الفرس», a horse-cloth, matching مجللا], I have come to wearing the face-veil for fear of the heat and the wind.

dervis-irab:15-26.t:
* I'rab:
(هَلْ أَتاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسى) A resumptive utterance, intended to console the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over his people's denial of him. هل has the meaning of قد; it is also said to be a question of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), the meaning being "Has the story of Moses not come to you?". أتاك: a past verb and a direct object; حديث موسى: the agent. (إِذْ ناداهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوىً) إذ is an adverb of past time, attached to حديث موسى and not to أتاك as one might imagine, because their times differ; the clause ناداه is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; ناداه: a past verb and a direct object; ربه: the agent; بالواد: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ناداه; the yāʾ of الوادي was dropped to follow the written form of the muṣḥaf; المقدس is an adjective of الوادي and طوى a badal (substitute); the discussion of it has been given at length before. It was read with tanwīn and without it. al-Jawharī said: «طوى is the name of a place in al-Shām; its ṭāʾ is pronounced with kasra or ḍamma; it is declined or diptote. Whoever declines it makes it the name of a valley and a place and makes it indefinite; whoever does not decline it makes it a town and a plot and makes it definite». (اذْهَبْ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغى) The clause is the content of an omitted saying, its implied form being "and He said: Go"; it is also possible that it is a clause explicating the calling (nidāʾ). إلى فرعون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اذهب; إن with its noun, and the clause طغى is its khabar; the clause إنه طغى is a reason for the command to go. (فَقُلْ هَلْ لَكَ إِلى أَنْ تَزَكَّى) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قل an imperative verb whose agent is latent, the implied form being "you"; هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is an offer (ʿarḍ), to invite him with gentleness, mildness and tactfulness; لك is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "inclination"; إلى أن تزكى: attached to the implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Have you an inclination to purification?", like "Have you an inclination for good?", i.e. "Have you an inclination toward good?". The origin of تزكى is تتزكى, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped, i.e. you purify yourself from polytheism. The interrogative clause is the content of what is said; and أن and what follows are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, genitive through إلى, as has been given. (وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلى رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشى) The wāw is a conjunction; أهديك is conjoined to تزكى, and the kāf is a direct object; إلى ربك: attached to أهديك; فتخشى is conjoined to أهديك. He made fear the goal of guidance because it is the pillar of the matter and the sum of piety; whenever a person fears his Lord, nothing issues from him but good. (فَأَراهُ الْآيَةَ الْكُبْرى) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted element, meaning "so he went, so he showed him"; أراه: «an imperfect verb» in the source [Translator's note: the verb is a past verb, not imperfect], its agent latent, the implied form being "he"; the hāʾ is the first object of أرى; الآية is the second object of أرى; الكبرى is an adjective of الآية, which is the turning of the staff into a serpent, or the hand. (فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصى) conjoined to what precedes. (ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعى) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; it was used because the voiding and undoing of faith requires a long time; the clause يسعى is a ḥāl from the pronoun in أدبر. (فَحَشَرَ فَنادى فَقالَ: أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلى) conjoined likewise; and the clause أنا ربكم الأعلى is the content of what is said. (فَأَخَذَهُ اللَّهُ نَكالَ الْآخِرَةِ وَالْأُولى) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أخذه الله: a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; نكال الآخرة والأولى is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), a maṣdar of أخذ; the figurative usage is either in the verb, i.e. "He made an example of him by seizing, the example of the Hereafter and the first", or in the maṣdar, i.e. "He seized him with a seizing of exemplary punishment". It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of making an example of him. al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to its being a confirming maṣdar; he said: «It is a confirming maṣdar, like وعد الله and صبغة الله, as if it were said: Allah made an example of him with the example of the Hereafter and the first». It is also possible that the accusative of نكال is by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with an example". al-Zajjāj preferred that it is a confirming maṣdar. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نكل به ينكل, of the pattern qatala, نكلة قبيحة: he afflicted him with a calamity; and نكل به with tashdīd is intensive; the noun is النكال». الآخرة والأولى are two adjectives of the two words of Pharaoh. The last word is his saying «أنا ربكم الأعلى», and the first word is his saying before it «ما علمت لكم من إله غيري», and between the two words, as has been said, were forty years. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشى) إن is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is the fronted khabar of إن; the lām is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) that gives emphasis; عبرة is the postponed noun of إن; لمن is an adjective of عبرة, and the clause يخشى is the ṣila of من.

dervis-irab:27-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَمْكَها) its raising. One says سمك يسمك, of the pattern naṣara, the thing: he raised it; and one says "Allah raised the heaven (سمك الله السماء)". al-Farazdaq said:
إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا ... بيتا دعائمه أعزّ وأطول
(He who raised the heaven built for us a house whose pillars are mightier and taller.)
السمك is the maṣdar of سمك; it is also the ceiling, or the span from the top of the house to its bottom, and the stature of anything.
(فَسَوَّاها) He made it level and smooth, with no elevation or depression in it.
(وَأَغْطَشَ) In al-Qāmūs: «غطش the night, يغطش, of the pattern ḍaraba: it grew dark, like أغطش; and Allah أغطشه». al-Rāghib said: «Its origin is from الأغطش, the one with weak sight in his eye, and التغاطش is feigning blindness». One says أغطش الليل intransitively, like أظلم; so أفعل here is both transitive and intransitive.
(دَحاها) دحا the earth, يدحوها, دحوا, and دحى يدحى: i.e. he spread it and stretched it out; it is among the verbs with wāw and yāʾ (as the third radical), so it is written with alif and with yāʾ.

* I'rab:
(أَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقاً أَمِ السَّماءُ بَناها) The hamza is for a question of rebuke and reproach; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, أشد a khabar and خلقا a tamyīz; أم is a conjunction and السماء is conjoined to أنتم; the clause بناها is a ḥāl, as if it were an explanation of the manner of its creation; it may be explicative, with no grammatical position; and it is also possible to parse السماء as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "stronger in creation". (رَفَعَ سَمْكَها فَسَوَّاها) The clause is a badal (substitute) of the clause بناها, following it; رفع سمكها: a past verb, a direct object and a latent agent, the implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; فسواها is conjoined to رفع. (وَأَغْطَشَ لَيْلَها وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحاها) conjoined to what precedes; ليلها is the object of أغطش and ضحاها the object of أخرج. (وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ دَحاها) The wāw is a conjunction; الأرض is accusative by ishtighāl, by an omitted verb explained by what follows; بعد ذلك is an adverb attached to دحاها; and the clause دحاها is explicative. (أَخْرَجَ مِنْها ماءَها وَمَرْعاها) The clause is explicative of what is indispensable for the possibility of dwelling on it, namely arranging the matter of food and drink and the possibility of settling upon it; it may also be a ḥāl with an implied قد, i.e. "bringing forth", which is the view of most, although I incline to the first view. منها: attached to أخرج; ماءها a direct object and مرعاها conjoined to ماءها. المرعى here is a mīmī maṣdar with the sense of the passive. (وَالْجِبالَ أَرْساها) The wāw is a conjunction; الجبال is accusative by ishtighāl also, as before, and the clause is conjoined to the first. (مَتاعاً لَكُمْ وَلِأَنْعامِكُمْ) متاعا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "He did that to provide enjoyment for you"; Zāda in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī preferred that it be a maṣdar of its omitted verb indicated by the context, i.e. "We gave you enjoyment of it", which is not far-fetched; لكم is attached to متاعا; and ولأنعامكم is conjoined to لكم. (فَإِذا جاءَتِ الطَّامَّةُ الْكُبْرى) The fāʾ is a conjunction indicating that what follows depends on what precedes, as the word متاع suggests; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause جاءت is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; الطامة is the agent and الكبرى an adjective of الطامة. الطامة is the Resurrection. In al-Mukhtār: «A torrent came and طم the well, i.e. buried it and levelled it; and everything that became abundant until it rose and overcame has طم, of the pattern radda. One says "above every ṭāmma is a ṭāmma"; from it the Resurrection is called ṭāmma. الطم with kasra is dragging; one says "he came with الطم والرم", i.e. with abundant water». The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «الطامة is the calamity that overwhelms (تطم على) calamities, i.e. rises above and overcomes them. Among their proverbs: "the valley ran and overflowed (طم على) the villages". It is the Resurrection because it overwhelms every terror; and it is said to be the second blast». The apodosis of إذا is omitted, indicated by the detail mentioned, the implied form being "there came of the momentous matters what does not cross the mind, no eye has seen, and no ear has heard".
(يَوْمَ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ ما سَعى) يوم is a badal (substitute) of إذا, a partial substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull); the clause يتذكر is in the position of genitive by annexation, and the returning pronoun is omitted, the implied form being "on which man remembers"; you may also make it an exact substitute (badal muṭābiq), the whole for the whole, meaning: when he sees his deeds recorded in his book he remembers them, having forgotten them. الإنسان is the agent of يتذكر, and ما is relative or maṣdarī. (وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِمَنْ يَرى) conjoined to جاءت; برزت is a passive past verb and الجحيم a deputy agent; لمن: attached to برزت; and the clause يرى has no position, being a ṣila of من. (فَأَمَّا مَنْ طَغى وَآثَرَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the utterance is resumptive, intended to explain the condition of people in this world; for this reason making the fāʾ the apodosis of إذا is weak and inadmissible. أما is a particle of condition and detail; من a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause طغى has no position; آثر is conjoined to طغى; الحياة is a direct object and الدنيا an adjective of الحياة; the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of أما; إن is a particle resembling the verb, الجحيم its noun, and هي a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; المأوى is the khabar of إن, and the clause is the khabar of من. The al in المأوى is a substitute for the pronoun referring to من; it is also said that the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "it is the abode for him"; the first is the view of the Kufans and the second the view of the Basrans. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوى فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوى) The clause is conjoined to the preceding clause. The wording of al-Rāzī: «These two attributes are the opposites of the two preceding attributes: His saying "But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord" is the opposite of His saying "As for him who transgressed", and His saying "and restrained the soul from desire" is the opposite of "and preferred the life of this world". As all ugly deeds are included in those two attributes, so all acts of obedience are included in these two.» (يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْساها) The clause is resumptive, intended to relate another kind of their obstinacy. يسألونك: an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object; عن الساعة: attached to يسألونك; أيان is an interrogative noun, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مرساها is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause has no position, because it is an explanation of their question about the Hour, i.e. "when is its anchoring (irsāʾ)?", i.e. its establishing and fixing, or its end and resting-place, from the مرسى of the ship, which is where it arrives and where it settles. (فِيمَ أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْراها) فيم is a fronted khabar, and the dropping of the alif of the interrogative ما when preceded by a preposition has already been given; أنت is a postponed mubtadaʾ; من ذكراها is attached to what the khabar is attached to; the meaning is "in what part of its mention are you?"; the clause has no position, as if it were a denial and rejection of their question about the Hour and a statement of the falsity of the question. It is also said: فيم is a denial of their question, and what follows is a resumption giving the reason for the denial, i.e. "Why this question?", then a new start is made and it is said "you are of its mention (أنت من ذكراها)"; so فيم is not a fronted khabar of what follows but the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Why this question that comes from the disbelievers?", and the speech is complete at that point in his view; then he resumes with the clause أنت من ذكراها as an explanation of the reason for the denial of their question, as if it were said: "It is near, not far, because you are one of its signs, so your being sent is enough evidence for them of its nearness and of the concern to prepare for it, so there is no sense in their asking about it". The meaning of أنت من ذكراها is "you are among its signs and reminders". (إِلى رَبِّكَ مُنْتَهاها) إلى ربك is a fronted khabar and منتهاها a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. (إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرُ مَنْ يَخْشاها) إنما is restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); أنت is a mubtadaʾ, منذر a khabar and من a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause يخشاها is the ṣila of من, with no position. (كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَها لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحاها) كأن with its noun; يوم is an adverb of time attached to the sense of simile contained in كأن; the clause يرونها is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; the clause لم يلبثوا is the khabar of كأنهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; عشية is an adverb of time attached to يلبثوا; أو is a conjunction; and ضحاها is conjoined to عشية. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: how is the annexation of الضحى to العشية sound? I say: because of the relation between them, since they meet in one day. If you say: why was it not said "except an evening or a forenoon", and what is the benefit of annexation? I say: to indicate that the duration of their stay seemed not to reach a whole day, but an hour of it, its evening or its forenoon; so when the day was left out, he annexed it to its evening. It is like His saying "they stayed only an hour of a day".»

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها» there is a loose trope (majāz mursal), because المرعى (pasture) is applied to what people eat, so المرعى was used for any food, of man and others; the relation is the use of the restricted for the unrestricted. It could also be an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), in that people's eating is likened to the grazing of beasts, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: «By مرعاها He meant what people and cattle eat; grazing was borrowed for man as roaming (الرتع) was borrowed in His saying "we shall roam and play".»
2- In His saying «فأما من طغى وآثر الحياة الدنيا فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه ونهى النفس عن الهوى فإن الجنة هي المأوى» there is the art of antithesis (muqābala); the wording of al-Rāzī on this point has been given.
3- In His saying «أيان مرساها» there is an explicit metaphor, for he borrowed إرساء (anchoring), which is used only of what has weight.
